title: Finite and integral point duality normalized by actual derived evaluation
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$, as in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Let $(R,B)$ be $(A_{E,n},(A_{E,n})_s)$ or $(\mathcal O_E,\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s})$, with constant and completed coefficient sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$. For an $R$-module $M$ put $L_RM=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M$, with sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], applied termwise to complexes. Then $L_R$ and $\Gamma(s,-)$ are exact, and $\Gamma(s,B)=R$ through the constant-value map. Their adjunction sends $h:L_RM\to V$ to $m\mapsto h_s(1\otimes m)$, with inverse $t\mapsto(b\otimes m\mapsto b\,t(m)|_U)$ on each site object $U$.
For every $C\in D^b_{ctf}(s,R)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], set $F=\operatorname{Fib}_s=\Gamma(s,-)$ and $c=FC$. The actual unit $c\to\Gamma(s,L_Rc)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $L_Rc$ is bounded constructible, and the actual counit $L_Rc\to C$ is an isomorphism. Integrally $c$ admits a bounded finite-projective representative $P$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], and $L_RP$ is a constructible representative of $C$ through this counit.
Use the derived tensor and Hom of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Put $H=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,B)$ and $c^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(c,R)$. Let $\kappa_C:FH\to c^\vee$ be the coefficient tensor–Hom transpose of $F(\operatorname{ev}_{C,B})$ through the unit and tensor comparisons of [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor]. Then $\kappa_C$ is an isomorphism. On the counit model it is the derived Hom-complex comparison $q:h\mapsto(x\mapsto h(1\otimes x))$ into a K-injective resolution of $B$; finite coefficients allow a K-flat flat-term representative of $c$, and integral coefficients allow the perfect model $P$. K-flatness, K-injectivity and signed Hom complexes are those of [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pur-kinjective-complex, def-pur-hom-complex]. With factors ordered $c\otimes\operatorname{Hom}$, evaluation on degrees $p,j$ is $(-1)^{pj}h(1\otimes x)$. The integral assertion concerns the specified completed tensor and its evaluation, not just ordinary ambient tensor.
Let $u:\omega_{s,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ be the identity-adjunction isomorphism, $D_sC=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\omega_{s,R})$, $\rho_C=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,u)$, and $j_C:F(D_sC)\to c^\vee$ the specified isomorphism of [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex]. Then $j_C=\kappa_C\circ F(\rho_C)$ as derived morphisms, naturally in $C$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pod-point-exact-extension-sections] to the two coefficient pairs in the statement. It gives exact $L_R$ and $F=\Gamma_s$, the constant-value ring isomorphism $R\to FB$, and the adjunction with exactly the two stated formulas. Its unit is $m\mapsto1\otimes m$, and its counit multiplies restricted sections. The termwise formulas commute with differentials and homotopies, so they are the maps used below.

proof.text: For the given $C\in D^b_{ctf}(s,R)\subset D^b_c(s,R)$, [lem-weil-point-sections-finiteness] gives bounded finite cohomology of $c=FC$ at finite coefficients and bounded finitely generated cohomology integrally. The hypotheses of [lem-pod-point-sections-reconstruction] are supplied by step 1. That lemma gives the actual quasi-isomorphism $\eta_c:c\to FL_Rc$, constructibility of $L_Rc$, and the actual counit isomorphism $\epsilon_C:L_Rc\to C$. Integrally it also supplies a bounded finite-projective representative $P$ of $c$ and the constructible model $L_RP$ of $C$ through $\epsilon_C$. These are specified adjunction maps, rather than an arbitrary choice of point equivalence.

source.place: Second sentence, expanded point Hom calculation and normalization of its actual evaluation; agent argument using the cited nodes.

proof.text: At finite coefficients choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $Q\to c$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the one-object ringed site with ring $R$. Integrally use $P$ from step 2, which is bounded finite-projective and hence is a permitted perfect model in [lem-pod-point-completed-evaluation]. Choose $B\to I$ K-injective by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], on the small pro-etale site in the fixed universe. Apply [lem-pod-point-derived-hom-evaluation] with the exact adjunction of step 1 (and with a flat-term K-flat resolution also integrally if desired). It identifies $F\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(L_RQ,I)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(Q,FI)$ by $q(h)(x)=h(1\otimes x)$, makes $FI$ a K-injective resolution of $R$, and gives an isomorphism $q_C:FH\to c^\vee$ after transport through $\epsilon_C$. Thus $q_C$ is a derived morphism, independent of resolutions and natural in $C$.

source.place: Second sentence, expanded point Hom calculation and normalization of its actual evaluation; agent argument using the cited nodes.

proof.text: At finite coefficients, [lem-pod-point-derived-hom-evaluation] gives the ordinary evaluation square for $q$. Its inverse tensor comparison sends $x\otimes h$ to $(1\otimes x)\otimes h$ by [lem-sf-point-ringed-evaluation-model]; the finite-stage comparison is this representative comparison by [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor]. Consequently both routes from $c\otimes_R^LFH$ to $R$ send homogeneous $x\in Q^p$ and $h$ of degree $j$ to $(-1)^{pj}h(1\otimes x)$. In derived notation, writing $\tau:F(C\otimes_B^LH)\to c\otimes_R^LFH$ for that comparison, this says $F(\operatorname{ev}_{C,B})\tau^{-1}=\operatorname{ev}_{c,R}(1_c\otimes q_C)$. The tensor-Hom adjunction defining $\kappa_C$ in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] is a bijection on morphisms: the displayed equality therefore gives $\kappa_C=q_C$. In particular $\kappa_C$ is an isomorphism at finite coefficients.

source.place: Second sentence, expanded point Hom calculation and normalization of its actual evaluation; agent argument using the cited nodes.

proof.text: Integrally put $J=L_R(\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,R))$. Apply [lem-pod-point-completed-evaluation] to the bounded finite-projective $P$ of step 2. It identifies $J\cong H$ on the counit model and states the equality $F(\widehat{\operatorname{ev}})=\operatorname{ev}_{P,R}(1_P\otimes q_P)\tau$, where $\tau:F(L_RP\widehat\otimes_R^LJ)\to P\otimes_R^LFJ$ is the specified completed point comparison. In particular this equality uses the prescribed quotient coordinates and zero shifted-product coordinate of completion. Precompose by $\tau^{-1}$ and transpose under the coefficient tensor-Hom adjunction. This gives $\kappa_C=q_P$, after the counit identification and $P\cong c$. Here $q_P$ is the Hom comparison of step 3, hence invertible. This proves the completed assertion, with the same signed evaluation formula; it does not infer a completed equality merely from the ambient tensor calculation.

source.place: Second sentence, expanded point Hom calculation and normalization of its actual evaluation; agent argument using the cited nodes.

proof.text: Use [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex] for the identity-adjunction isomorphism $u:\omega_{s,R}\to B$ and its canonical evaluated coefficient duality isomorphism $j_C$. To compute that specified identification, first apply $R\mathcal Hom_s(C,u)$ to identify the dualizing target with $B$, then compute its point internal Hom on the counit model as in step 3. On a homogeneous Hom component $h$ this composite has value $x\mapsto u(h(1\otimes x))$: postcomposition with $u$ is $\rho_C$, and the second operation is $q_C$. This is exactly the coefficient-dual identification $j_C$, so $j_C=q_C\circ F(\rho_C)$. Steps 4 and 5 identify $q_C=\kappa_C$ for the actual finite and completed evaluations, giving the required equality of derived morphisms. The adjunction, counit, Hom comparison and completed evaluation used here are natural by the cited statements. Precomposition by an input arrow commutes with postcomposition by $u$ and with $h\mapsto h(1\otimes -)$, hence the equality is natural in $C$.

I read every cited statement in full. Step 1: lem-pod-point-exact-extension-sections is exactly paragraph 1. Step 2: sections-finiteness (1)/(2) with D^b_ctf in D^b_c meets the hypotheses of sections-reconstruction, which gives the actual unit and counit and the integral P. Step 3: derived-hom-evaluation needs a flat-term K-flat model of c (kflat-resolution at finite level, the bounded finite-projective P integrally) and a K-injective B->I (the site is small); it gives the q isomorphism and the K-injective FI. Step 4: ringed-evaluation-model plus def-sf-point-fibre-tensor-finite-models pin the finite tau to the x(x)y -> section-tensor rule. So F(ev)tau^-1 = ev(1(x)q_C), and transpose injectivity gives kappa_C = q_C, with sign (-1)^{pj}. Step 5: completed-evaluation applies to P with the same completed tau; it gives Gamma(ev^) = ev(1(x)q_P)tau, hence kappa_C = q_P. Step 6: j_C = q_C o F(rho_C) is exactly the construction in dualizing-complex proof steps 1 and 3 (u = Phi(1), then q on C = L_R c). Edge cases: C=0, C=B[0] (kappa = id = q), C=B[1] (sign -1), integral O_E/varpi (two-term P), n=1 (no regularity needed). No proof_dep reaches the item, so there is no cycle. Advisory: lem-coef-finite-point-internal-hom-evaluation overlaps the finite-level kappa clause under the nu-counit normalization of omega; it is not a duplicate of the item. Also, dualizing-complex pins j only in its proof (known from Q14/Q152). Batch 5: sections-reconstruction (reaching sections-derived-reduction) and ringed-evaluation-model (reaching def-trf-geometric-morphism) are both already in the base batch-5 closure, and so are all 11 new proof_deps; the closure gains nothing.
